There is a photo inside this sound.

SSTV converts the brightness and colour of a photo into audio tones. The receiver measures these tones and rebuilds the image line by line.

This experiment uses Robot36: a 320 × 240 colour image is sent in about 37 seconds together with a start signal. Other SSTV modes are not supported in this first version.

On the phone, open the microphone first, then play the whole sound from the other device. Keep the phone close to the speaker, avoid excessive volume and background music. Keep the screen on during the transfer.

Photo selection and sound decoding happen on your device. The app never uploads your photo or microphone audio to a server. Loading the page requires the internet once; the photo transfer itself happens over sound. After installation the app works fully offline.

Four ways to move a photo

Sound — the classic acoustic path. Works between any two devices with a speaker and a microphone, no pairing needed.

QR code — the photo is split into consecutive QR codes; the other device reads them with its camera. Silent and fully offline.

Bluetooth — the photo travels over Bluetooth LE between two Web Bluetooth devices, or the acoustic transfer plays on a Bluetooth speaker.

NFC — a tap pairs the phones and opens the right role on each one.

About the counters

The counters in the header are kept by a free counter service. They show the approximate number of different browsers and reception attempts; they do not measure unique people. The attempt counter increases when listening with the microphone starts successfully. A half-finished or missing image still counts; a completed one is not counted twice. If the microphone cannot open, no attempt is added. Offline, the counters are hidden.

Languages

The interface speaks Turkish, English, German, Spanish, French, Arabic (right-to-left) and Simplified Chinese. Translations live in standard GNU gettext files (.po source, .mo compiled) under locales/ — send a pull request to add yours.
